summary: Customer wants an optical measurement during yeast fermentation to follow growth and detect changes earlier, mentioning a biomass signal and a metabolic signal that are not yet defined as separate targets; they ask for help shaping an initial feasibility study with useful reference measurements.

facts_stated.text: We would like an optical measurement during yeast fermentation to help us follow growth and notice changes earlier
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: an optical measurement during yeast fermentation

process.value: broth becomes more optically dense as the run develops
process.enquiry_quote: broth becomes more optically dense as the run develops

customer_premises.claim: An optical measurement will let them follow growth and notice changes earlier
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: help us follow growth and notice changes earlier

customer_premises.claim: Both a biomass signal and a metabolic signal exist as usable signals, even though neither is defined as a target
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: both a biomass signal and a metabolic signal, but these have not been defined as separate targets

customer_premises.claim: The request can be turned into an initial feasibility study with useful reference measurements before deciding facts are known
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: help turning this request into an initial feasibility study with useful reference measurements

unknowns: Biomass target: which species or variable, and the required measurement range
Metabolic target: which species or variable; whether it is a fluorescent species
Matrix composition and interferences in the fermentation broth
Optical behaviour of the broth: scattering versus absorption, absolute turbidity
Installation point, probe interface and optical path length
Required accuracy, detection limit and response time
Reference method for comparison and the current method whose timing must be beaten
Organism/strain, fermenter scale and run duration or timeline
